unit: Unit 12: Everyday Life with Your Computer
title: Calendar and Reminders
drDigitalIntro:
A calendar holds things that happen at a time. A reminder holds things you need to do. Your computer keeps both.

- Click a day, then create an event and give it a name and a time. That is the whole job.
- Reminders are simpler: type what you need to remember, and tick it off when it is done.
- Both live on your computer rather than in your head, which is the entire point.
- If you use the same account on a phone, what you add here shows up there too.
- The common mistake is putting a to-do on the calendar. If it has no particular time, it belongs in reminders.

playgroundTask.goal: You put an appointment on the calendar and a task in your reminders

steps.say: Buying milk has no set time, so it belongs in reminders. Switch over to Reminders.
You picked up the milk — tick it off.

drDigitalSuccess: That is the difference in practice: the appointment went on the calendar because it happens at 2:00, and the milk went in reminders because it just needs doing. Keep them separate and both stay useful.
drDigitalHint: Start by clicking Wednesday in the calendar grid. To swap between the calendar and your reminders, use the buttons at the top.
